source.title: Quantifying Prior Dominance in RAG Systems

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or document mismatch; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates downstream QA extraction across model sizes and reports task outcomes, using accuracy and context-utilization measures rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy or fitted scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study cites pretraining scaling laws but does not measure held-out pretraining loss, training-token or compute scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its reported extraction accuracy and NCU results across model sizes bear on V6. The conflict percentages in Table 1 are also described as prior-override rates in the text and Figure 5A; they are recorded once. Latency is not a downstream performance measure for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates three Qwen2.5-Instruct sizes (1.5B, 7B, 72B) on factual-extraction QA under zero-shot, oracle and noise contexts. It argues that downstream gains with scale show 'extreme diminishing returns', which bears on V6. It does not measure pretraining loss, fit any curve or vary training, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim that prior dominance correlates with model scale (the 7B to 72B jump) and with proprietary alignment (the 'Alignment Tax' hypothesis). They frame all claims as limited to strict short-answer extraction without CoT.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates prompted RAG extraction outcomes across selected model sizes; it does not train models or fit held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling laws, extrapolate runs, or optimize parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model size and context condition (zero-shot, oracle, semantic noise, adversarial conflict). No fitting-method sensitivity is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: The parametric override rate under fabricated-entity conflicts is similar at 1.5B and 7B (34.9%, 33.1%) and higher at 72B (42.5%); gpt-4o-mini is 47.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger models more often override contradictory retrieved context in favour of parametric knowledge (prior dominance grows with scale).

fits_no_version.finding: Raw NCU goes negative and the negative-transfer rate (confidence loss below zero-shot) is 3.8–4.8% for Qwen models vs 9.8% for gpt-4o-mini.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retrieved context can reduce model confidence below the zero-shot baseline, at rates that vary by model.

record.problems: Only three sizes from one open-weight model family support the size comparison; no scaling curve is fitted. The commercial API has unstated size and is acknowledged as not directly comparable. The evaluation is limited to English factual extraction with a 5-token generation limit and synthetic adversarial conflicts. No uncertainty estimates or statistical-test results are reported, despite the paper's reference to statistical parity.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or power-law fit.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes.
No fitted predictive relation, no link to pretraining loss, only three sizes in one family, and only short-answer English extraction QA; reasoning and CoT tasks are excluded.

record.verdict_notes: The 'success' metric is the length-normalized probability of the gold answer exceeding 0.05, not exact match of the generation. The 72B model was quantized while the smaller models ran in float16, which confounds the size comparison. Only three sizes, no seeds, and no confidence intervals, although the paper claims 'statistical parity'. The paper's Qwen2.5 citation points to the Qwen3 report. The latency column is excluded correctly.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy or power-law fit in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token trends.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law form across other modalities or training regimes.

Measures strict English factual-extraction/RAG QA outcomes across selected models, not a fitted predictive relationship, pretraining-loss relationship, or broad set of downstream tasks. The proprietary API has no stated parameter count, so it cannot be placed on the reported size sequence.
No comparison of scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or curve shapes.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: Zero-shot success is non-monotonic: 53.6%, 51.9%, 55.9% (R01–R03). The largest model improves modestly over the smallest, while the intermediate model declines.

relation.reason: Its intra-family size comparisons directly test downstream improvement with scale under V6.

tranche.reason: The study explicitly argues that parameter scaling has severe diminishing returns in strict factual extraction and reports flat or declining extraction measures across model sizes.

source_check.notes: Results concern English factual extraction with at most five generated tokens, without CoT. The 72B model is quantized; uncertainty and a statistical test supporting the claimed parity are not reported. Bounded NCU measures normalized confidence gain, distinct from extraction success.

statements.correction: Oracle success: 95.9%, 92.3%, 91.8% for Qwen2.5-Instruct 1.5B, 7B, 72B respectively (Table 1; R05–R07). The 72B model used quantized precision; smaller models used float16 (Section 4.2).
statements.problem: The oracle extraction numbers and quantization qualification are correct, but the cited rows R01–R03 contain zero-shot results.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Qwen2.5 family, strict factual extraction across zero-shot, oracle, and semantic-noise conditions
reader_labels.reason: Across the reported size sequence, oracle and noise extraction accuracy is lower for the 7B and 72B models than for the 1.5B model; bounded NCU is nearly unchanged rather than increasing with size (R01–R03, R05–R07, R09–R11, R17–R19). The study does not fit a predictive scale curve.
